headline: Bot-security company DataDome says Meta's new Muse agent produced a third of all AI browser-agent traffic it saw in September, despite only nine days of measurement.
score_reason: Vendor data, unaudited, with no stated network size; a selling point for its own security products.
importance_line: Website owners may find that traffic from cloud-run agents like Muse looks like data-centre traffic and slips past checks that trust home connections, but all figures are DataDome's own and unverified.
summary: PPC Land reports that DataDome's Q3 2026 AI Traffic Report counts nearly 25 billion AI agent requests across its network, up 41.5% from the second quarter, and that Meta's Muse agent made up 33% of agentic browser requests in September. Because Muse runs in its own cloud virtual machine, 99.3% of its sampled requests came from cloud and CDN networks, so home-connection checks will not spot it; PPC Land stresses that DataDome sells such tools, has not had its numbers audited and does not state how many sites its network covers.
